Built-in Platforms

A platform decides what to render. The matrix below shows which optional capabilities each platform implements; each section documents its options, which a program sets as props on the target in its output block, or --opt key=value sets from the command line.

Global Options

Declared by the standard library and set on output itself; accepted by every target.

Name Type Description
name string Display name for the app; used as window title and platform-native app name.
icon string Path to a launcher / favicon icon (SVG or PNG), relative to the project dir.
description string Short app description (Android description, HTML <meta description>, etc.).
version string Semantic version string (Android versionName, HTML meta, etc.).
maps bool When true, generate source maps for target languages that support them (Go //line directives, JS .map sidecars).
test bool When true, the generator emits unit tests in the target language alongside the application code, using that language's native test runner (Go's testing, Kotlin's JUnit, JS's Jest/Vitest).
targets type

android

Android app. Emits Jetpack Compose; can mix in Go via gomobile when --lang go is used.

Supported languages: go, kotlin

Options

Name Type Description
package string Kotlin package / Android application ID.
appName string Display name used in AndroidManifest.xml.
icon string Path to a launcher icon asset.
main bool Emit a full Gradle project or just Compose sources.
gradle option Build through Gradle (true), without it (false), or choose (null): a generated project is a Gradle one, to open in Android Studio, and `sngl build` and `sngl run` build without Gradle or a JVM, except a Go program or a test, which still need Gradle.
color string Theme accent color (hex).
projectDir string Absolute path to the project root. Set automatically by `sngl generate`; used to resolve relative asset paths.
testRunner string Which Android runtime to test against under `sngl test`. "robolectric": JVM simulation, fast, no emulator (default). "device": APK on a real emulator/device via adb.
toolchain string Toolchain combo — a known-good set of Gradle/AGP/Kotlin/Compose/SDK versions (see internal/androidtc). "stable" (default) or "next".
sdk int Override compileSdk / targetSdk (0 = combo default).
minSdk int Override minSdk (0 = default 26).
gradleVersion string Override the Gradle distribution version (unset = combo default).
reservedNames list What its generated code introduces beside a program's names: the types, locals and parameters the screen itself declares, and `Toast`, which the language's Alert intrinsic writes as text. A Compose name the screen imports is not here: each is imported through the file's import set, which aliases it around a program's own declaration of that name.

bubbletea

Terminal UI, written in Go using the Bubble Tea framework.

Supported languages: go

Options

Name Type Description
package string Go package name for the generated files.
main bool Emit a standalone main() or a library-style module.
tests bool Emit companion test files (default: true; set "false" to skip).
reservedNames list What its generated code introduces beside a program's names: the packages it imports, the Model's own fields and the getters and setters a var named `view`, `update`, `init` or `terminalSize` would collide with, and the locals Update and View declare around the handler and view code they hold.

fyne

Cross-platform desktop GUI, written in Go using Fyne.

Supported languages: go, none

Options

Name Type Description
package string Go package name for the generated files.
main bool Emit a standalone main() or a library-style module.
reservedNames list What its generated code introduces beside a program's names: the packages it imports, an instance record's receiver, the Model's own members, and the locals BuildUI declares around the nodes a program names.

gtk4

Native Linux/GNOME desktop GUI using GTK4.

Supported languages: go

Options

Name Type Description
package string Go package name for the generated files.
main bool Emit a standalone main() or a library-style module.
gir string Which introspection data to read the widget vocabulary from: "builtin" for the bundled subset, a path to a `Gtk-4.0.gir`, or unset to probe the system locations and fall back to the bundled subset.
cgo bool Make, fill and write a GIR class through the C functions GTK names, from the generated file itself, rather than through pkg/go/gtk4rt. Every string handed to GTK is then the generated code's own, and the file builds with cgo whatever it renders.
reservedNames list What its generated code introduces beside a program's names: the packages it imports -- `C` is cgo's, which a Go export of `c` would be -- an instance record's receiver, the Model's own members, and the locals and helpers its application code declares.

html

Web output. Static site by default, or a language-driven HTTP server when paired with a language that implements HTTPCompiler.

Supported languages: go, none

Options

Name Type Description
preview bool Render in preview mode (iframe-friendly; stable element IDs for live reload).
test bool Emit a test harness instead of the normal app bundle.
stylesheet string Relative path to a CSS file included in every page.
projectDir string Absolute path to the project root. Set automatically by `sngl generate`; used to resolve relative asset paths.
package string Route mode: target Go package name (default "ui", or "main" when main=true).
main bool Route mode: emit a main() that calls ListenAndServe.
framework string Route mode: HTTP framework (default "net/http").
listen string Host:port `sngl run` listens on: the static server's, ":0" when empty, or the route server's, ":8080" when empty.
minify bool Minify emitted HTML and inline JS via esbuild.
noCacheBust bool Disable content-hash filenames for emitted assets; produce stable paths.
reservedNames list Its page script is JavaScript whatever the language, so it reserves JavaScript's words, and beside them what the script introduces: the `state` object a page's vars live in, a factory's `props`, the `String` it redefines, and the browser globals it calls.

none

Headless execution in the interpreter, which generates no code.

Supported languages:
